name: Barbell Dead Hang
description: The barbell dead hang involves gripping a loaded barbell in the rack or on the floor from a standing position and holding it for time. Unlike a pull-up bar hang, the arms remain straight and the body stands, loading the grip and forearm flexors isometrically with heavy weights. It directly trains the grip strength needed for deadlifts and other heavy pulling movements. It is typically performed with deadlift-level loads at the end of a training session.

execution.starting_position: Load a barbell at hip height in a rack. Stand and grasp the bar with a double overhand grip, shoulder-width.
execution.setup_instructions: Set the bar at deadlift height. Use loads at or above your deadlift working weight for grip training specificity.
steps: Step 1: Grip the barbell with a double overhand grip.
Step 2: Lift the bar off the pins or take it from the floor.
Step 3: Hold it in a standing position with arms fully extended for the prescribed duration.
Step 4: Set the bar down when grip is about to fail.
common_mistakes: Using straps (negates the grip training purpose)
Holding past the point of technique breakdown
safety_considerations: Ensure the bar is secured and the hold is performed over a rubber-matted platform
coaching_cues: Control when you set it down
